name: Heightpill / height blackpill
lead: The heightpill (or height blackpill) is a belief, widespread on looksmaxxing and incel-adjacent forums, that a man's height is among the most decisive factors in dating and social outcomes, and that short stature cannot be offset by other traits. The term follows the "pill" vocabulary of online manosphere communities, where a "pill" is a supposedly uncomfortable truth.

Adherents commonly describe a threshold, often framed in feet and inches, below which they say a man is at a major disadvantage.[1] Published research gives a more mixed picture: studies report that many women prefer taller male partners and that shorter men are rated less favourably on average, while other work finds that people trade height off against other traits and that preferences vary across cultures.[2][3]
infobox: Height preferences studied; the strong form of the claim is not established

paras: The heightpill holds that height functions as a gatekeeping trait. Forum posts describe being below a given height as a lasting social handicap, and some state that average height is no longer "enough".[1] Related terms in these communities include "manlet" for a short man, and discussions often rank height alongside face, frame and race as fixed traits that cannot be changed by effort.

Sociological and economic literature on height discrimination ("heightism", coined in 1971) reports that taller men were more likely to marry and have more children in several historical datasets, and that American women in one widely cited study preferred taller partners, with shorter men needing higher incomes to be rated equally appealing. In the same literature, average-height and tall men were rated similarly, with shorter men viewed less favourably.[2]

The same source reports that people trade height off against other qualities: an Indonesian study found men compensated for shorter stature with higher wages and women with more education, a Hungarian survey found most respondents favoured average to moderately tall heights, and a study of the Hadza foragers found height did not factor into mate choice, which the article takes to indicate that the preference is shaped by culture.[2]

Beyond dating, studies cited in reference works report that height correlates positively with income and occupational success in many settings, though part of the gap may be explained by sex or socioeconomic status.[2][3]

Communities that hold the heightpill discuss responses such as limb-lengthening surgery, growth hormone in adolescence, and footwear, as well as posture and "height-maxxing" techniques. Forum posts note that some teenagers consider growth hormone ineffective once their expected final height is set.[1] Medical sources on these methods are covered in their own entries.
No studies found testing the heightpill as a theory. Observational and survey studies of height and partner preference, summarised above, exist in the wider literature on height discrimination.[2]

timeline.event: Sociologist Saul Feldman coins the term "heightism" for height-based discrimination.[2]

lore.intro: On looksmaxxing forums the heightpill is treated as one of the main "pills", and threads on it recur frequently.[1]

claims.claim: Height is the single most decisive trait for a man's dating success.
claims.believers: Posters say that short men are overlooked regardless of face or effort, and describe a minimum height "threshold" that has risen in recent years.[1]
claims.experts: Studies report that many women prefer taller partners and that shorter men are rated less favourably, but also that people trade height against income, education and other traits, and that average-height and tall men were rated similarly.[2]

claims.claim: Looks or other traits cannot compensate for being short.
claims.believers: Forum users argue that good facial looks do not make up for a lack of height.[1]
claims.experts: Research summarised in reference works finds compensation: men with shorter stature offset it with higher wages in one Indonesian study.[2]

claims.claim: The importance of height is universal and biological.
claims.believers: Some posters describe a taller-is-better preference as instinctive and inherent to humans.
claims.experts: A study of Hadza foragers found height did not factor into mate choice, and the heightism literature notes the link between height and attractiveness reflects modern cultural norms and is not universal.[2]

card.summary: The belief that height decides a man's dating fate; research shows a taller-partner preference, not an iron rule.
card.note: Preferences are real in some studies but vary by culture and trade off against other traits.

quick.overview:
The heightpill is the belief that a man's height largely determines his dating and social success and that nothing else can fully make up for being short. It is a staple of looksmaxxing and blackpill forums.

Research reports that many women prefer taller men and that shorter men are rated less favourably on average, but people also trade height against income and education, and preferences differ across cultures.
quick.mechanism: It is a belief or framework rather than a practice. Believers treat height as a fixed trait; some respond with height-altering measures discussed in other entries.
quick.risks: The main documented concern in discussions is psychological distress among teens and men who fixate on height. Measures used to change height carry their own medical risks.
